thoughts.name: Who Was I?
thoughts.premise: There's a hole where your past should be. You keep reaching into it. The reaching itself hurts, and slows everything down.
thoughts.conclusion: You stop demanding the whole memory back and start letting it return in pieces, on its own terms. The hole is still there — but now you can stand at its edge without falling in.

whileForming.reason: The blank past gnaws at you.

whenInternalized.reason: You've made peace with the gap.
What the memory can't say, the gut now does.

thoughts.name: The Ledger Speaks
thoughts.premise: Numbers don't lie, but the people who write them do. You can't stop auditing every sentence you hear for the missing column.
thoughts.conclusion: You learn to hear the silence in a balance sheet — the deliberate omission, the rounded-off body. The city is a fraud, and you can finally read its books.

whileForming.reason: Everything is a transaction right now.

whenInternalized.reason: You see the load-bearing lie in any account.

thoughts.name: Everyone Is Drowning
thoughts.premise: Once you see how much quiet suffering this city runs on, you can't stop seeing it. It's hard to interrogate a man you've already forgiven.
thoughts.conclusion: You hold two truths at once: that everyone is drowning, and that some of them are holding others under. Compassion stops being a weakness and becomes a lens.

whileForming.reason: You can't bring yourself to lean on anyone.

whenInternalized.reason: You will never be feared, only trusted.

thoughts.name: The Body Remembers
thoughts.premise: Your hands know things — how to throw a punch, pick a lock, hold a man under. Your mind doesn't want to ask where they learned it.
thoughts.conclusion: You stop fighting the muscle memory and start trusting it. Whatever you were, the body kept the receipts.

whenInternalized.reason: The animal and the man finally cooperate.
You read a room the way a fighter does.

thoughts.name: The Drowned God
thoughts.premise: The Quarter says the flood didn't just take houses — it took something that was owed worship, and left a hunger in the water. Probably nonsense. You can't stop listening to the tide.
thoughts.conclusion: Believe it or not, the story is true *enough*: people act on it, kill for it, bail for it. You've learned to read the city's faith like evidence — because it is.

whileForming.reason: Reason keeps slipping under the waterline.

whenInternalized.reason: You feel the current of belief moving people.
You can speak the city's mythology back to it.

thoughts.name: Badge, or Man?
thoughts.premise: You carry a Watch badge you may not have earned, for an order that may not deserve you. Every choice asks the same question and you keep refusing to answer it.
thoughts.conclusion: You answer it. (Which way you answer sets a permanent stance the city — and the endings — will hold you to.)

whileForming.reason: You can't lead while you doubt the flag.

whenInternalized.reason: You finally know who you answer to.
